findings: RescalingCounterexample: at length 2/5, sparse-cut cost at most 70 bounds the only cut coordinate by 7/10 and leaves all pairs within length 2; volume zero rules out sparse cuts. At length 4/5, the cut 13/20 costs 65 and separates two feasible directed demand units at length 21/10. Thus expansion is genuinely not monotone under length increases.

RealParameterArboricity: integral walk lengths make the real threshold exactly equivalent to its natural floor for s nonnegative. For s at least 2 the floor is at least 2, floor(s) is at most s, and s is at most twice the floor. This gives 2/floor(s) at most 4/s. The n=0 case is explicit; n at least 1 permits monotonicity in the exponent. The returned actual forest partition inherits acyclicity, containment, and unique edge assignment, with both rounded and smooth ceiling bounds.
scope: The graph-level nonmonotonicity result does not by itself formalize an entire maximal sparse-cut sequence.

The literal real-s exact 2/s claim is contradicted by the elementary K_{a,a} family at s=5/2; this family argument was independently checked against arXiv v1, but is not claimed as a Lean theorem here.
The source even/odd discussion suggests intended integrality; the new module gives an explicit valid all-real repair.
